title: Opportunistic communication windows for heterogeneous multi-GPU inference scheduling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an opportunistic communication scheduler that inserts short non-blocking NCCL collectives and KV-cache prefetches into idle compute windows across heterogeneous multi-GPU stages. Aim is to reduce p99 latency and improve steady-state throughput without increasing tail due to blocking comms. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with kernel selection and runtime telemetry, and benchmarks on mixed A100/H100 fleets.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can detect sub-stage idle intervals and schedule non-blocking comms without delaying the critical prefill/decode path
End-to-end p99 token latency reduction >= 15% on a mixed 8-GPU (4xA100 + 4xH100) workload compared to baseline scheduler
No regression in correctness: outputs identical within existing tolerance; KV cache consistency preserved
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-stage comm overlap fraction, queued opportunistic ops, and per-request latency attribution
Automated regression test added to nightly multi-GPU harness and benchmark reproducible in CI
design_notes: Motivation: existing blocking NCCL stages create head-of-line delays on heterogeneous fleets where slower GPUs force others to wait. Many stages have micro idle periods (tens to hundreds of microseconds) that can be used for short collectives or prefetches.

Core idea: build a lightweight OpportunisticCommQueue (OCQ) that the conductor can schedule into available compute gaps. OCQ supports priorities (prefetch KV > small all-reduce metadata > low-priority model shard sync) and estimated duration metadata from kernel selector.

Integration with kernel selection: query kernel selector for expected stage compute duration distributions; use those distributions to identify safe insertion points and avoid disrupting prefill/decode SLOs.

Heterogeneity handling: track per-GPU instantaneous progress and bandwidth estimates; prefer scheduling comms on high-bandwidth links between fast GPUs while avoiding overlapping long NCCL ops on slow devices.
KV-cache prefetch: allow prefetch operations to be split into micro-prefetch units that align with OCQ windows to warm KV segments ahead of decode.

Fallbacks: if an opportunistic op would delay a critical token path beyond a configurable threshold, it is aborted and retried on next window. Also support a global budget to avoid starvation of critical comms.
API surface: runtime config flags (enable_opportunistic_comm, max_window_ms, per-op priority) and tracing hooks to attribute op scheduling decisions in Console.
Assumptions: accurate time accounting from GPUs for stage enter/exit; non-blocking NCCL primitives available on target kernels (ensure support across CUDA versions).
tradeoffs: Complexity vs gain: adds scheduler complexity and heuristics which could introduce subtle bugs; mitigated by conservative defaults and gradual rollout.

Prefetch accuracy: aggressive KV prefetch reduces decode stalls but may increase wasted memory/traffic for unused prefixes; solution: prioritize short, high-likelihood prefixes and make prefetch budgetable per-request.
Kernel selector reliance: improvements depend on accurate duration estimates — initial conservative estimates will be used, with online profiling to refine them.
Heterogeneous fairness: prioritizing fast links may starve slower devices; include tunable fairness parameters and global quotas.
risks: Mis-scheduled opportunistic comms could increase tail latency if estimation is off
Non-blocking NCCL semantics vary by CUDA/NCCL versions — potential portability issues
KV-cache prefetch correctness must be strongly validated to avoid stale/incorrect cache states
Telemetry noise may make it hard to interpret benefit without controlled benchmarks
test_plan: Microbenchmarks: inject synthetic compute/idle patterns to validate OCQ placement decisions deterministically
End-to-end benchmarks: run existing perf harness on mixed-fleet 8-GPU and 16-GPU topologies measuring p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and GPU utilization
A/B Canary: deploy runtime with opportunistic comms enabled for a small portion of traffic and compare request-level traces
Fault injection: simulate missed windows and aborted ops to ensure graceful recovery
Correctness: run regression evals and compare model outputs across baseline and opportunistic runs within tolerance thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement OCQ, basic scheduling heuristics, and unit tests in a feature branch; run microbenchmarks internally (2 engineers, 2 weeks)
Phase 2 (integration): integrate kernel selector hooks and KV-prefetch micro-ops; add telemetry and Console panels (canary across 5% of internal traffic)
Phase 3 (canary): enable for small external customers with monitoring and automatic rollback on regression alerts
Phase 4 (gradual rollout): increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with performance gates at each step
Phase 5 (optimize): tune heuristics using production telemetry and add ML-based window prediction if heuristics plateau
